GQA-001.question: What is the financial assistance provided under the Supporting Community Radio Movement in India scheme for?
GQA-001.reference_answer: The financial assistance is provided once the Community Radio Station (CRS) is made operational by the Licensee.
GQA-001.answer:
**Recommended Scheme**  
The **Supporting Community Radio Movement in India** scheme provides financial assistance to eligible organizations for setting up and operating Community Radio Stations (CRS).  

**Key Benefits & Eligibility**  
- Financial aid is given **once the CRS is operational** by the licensee.  
- The assistance aims to strengthen CRS in **remote and rural areas** to promote socio-economic and cultural development.  
- **Eligible entities** include NGOs, registered societies, public charitable trusts, and educational institutions that meet specific criteria.  

**Documents Needed**  
- Registration certificate (with translation if needed).  
- Memorandum of association/bye-laws (with translation if needed).  
- Balance sheets and auditor’s report for the last 3 years.  
- Map of service area, community profile, and geo-coordinates.  

**Next Steps**  
Check the official eligibility rules [1] and ensure your organization meets the criteria. If eligible, prepare the required documents and apply online [3].

GQA-002.question: What documents are required for the Production Linked Incentive Scheme For Automobile And Auto Component Industry application?
GQA-002.reference_answer: The required documents include Certificate of Incorporation, Memorandum & Articles of Association, PAN Card, Import Export Code (IEC) Registration Certificate, and a Letter of Authorization by Board of Directors or Managing Director.
GQA-002.answer:
**Documents Needed**  
To apply for the Production Linked Incentive Scheme for Automobile and Auto Component Industry, you will need to submit the following documents:  
- Certificate of Incorporation (Issued by ROC) [1]  
- Memorandum & Articles of Association (Submitted to ROC) [1]  
- PAN Card [1]  
- Import Export Code (IEC) Registration Certificate [1]  
- Letter of Authorization by Board of Directors or Managing Director or Equivalent [1]  
- Certificate from the Company Secretary of the Applicant / Managing Director for Credit History [1]  
- CIBIL Report of the Company [1]  
- Business Profile/ Corporate Presentation of the Applicant [1]  
- GST Registration Certificate [1]  
- Profile of Directors [1]  
- Annual Report of Holding Company [1]  
- Self-Certification on Revenue/ Investment/ Net worth from each of the Group Company (ies) [1]  

**Next Steps**  
Ensure all documents are ready and submit the application online via the portal [1]. For further assistance, contact the PMA at [pliauto.in/login].

GQA-003.question: What is the minimum percentage required for post-graduation in the National Centre for Communication Security (NCCS) Research Associates Scheme?
GQA-003.reference_answer: The minimum percentage required for post-graduation is 60%.
GQA-003.answer:
**Minimum Post-Graduation Percentage Requirement**  
For the National Centre for Communication Security (NCCS) Research Associates Scheme, the minimum post-graduation percentage required is **60%** in Electronics, Communications, Telecommunications, Information Technology, Computers, or related disciplines [1].  

**Key Eligibility Criteria**  
- Valid GATE score in relevant fields [1].  
- Post-graduation with a minimum of 60% marks and a valid GATE score at the time of admission [1].  
- PhD degree in relevant fields [1].  
- One year of work experience or a six-month internship certificate with NCCS/TEC [1].  

**Documents Required**  
- Mark-sheet of Class 10th / Date of Birth proof [1].  
- Mark-sheet of Engineering Graduation [1].  
- Mark-sheet of Engineering Post-Graduation (if applicable) [1].  
- GATE Score card (if available) [1].  
- Documentary proof of CGPA to Percentage conversion norm (if applicable) [1].  
- Work experience/Internship Certificate (if available) [1].  
- PhD Certificate (if applicable) [1].  

**Next Steps**  
Review the full eligibility criteria and prepare the required documents. If you meet the criteria, apply offline or online as per the scheme guidelines. [1]

GQA-004.reference_answer: The application process involves registering on the National Scholarship Portal, creating an application ID and password, logging in, and filling out the application form with required details and document uploads.

Financial Support To The Students Of N.E.R For Higher Professional Courses (NEC Merit Scholarship) [1]

GQA-005.question: What is the monthly stipend provided under the ICRO Amrit Internship Programme?
GQA-005.reference_answer: The selected intern is entitled to ₹ 6,000 per month as a stipend during the internship period.
GQA-005.answer:
**Monthly Stipend under ICRO Amrit Internship Programme**  
The ICRO Amrit Internship Programme provides a stipend of ₹ 6,000/- per month to selected interns during the internship period [1].  

**Key Benefits & Eligibility**  
- **Stipend**: ₹ 6,000/- per month [1].  
- **Certificate**: Interns receive an Internship Completion Certificate upon successful completion [1].  
- **Eligibility**: Applicants must be 12th Pass / Diploma Holder / Graduate or in the Final Year of graduation, aged 18–45 years, and a citizen of India [4].  

**Documents Needed**

- Passport size photo (JPG/JPEG, <2 MB)

To apply, provide your age and confirm if you are a Farmer or Student. Submit the required documents through the official portal [6].

GQA-006.question: What is the condition for a project to be considered under Pradhan Mantri Jan vikas karyakram?
GQA-006.reference_answer: The project area must have a minority population of more than 25% within a 15Km radius catchment area.
GQA-006.answer:
**Condition for a Project under PMJVK**  
To be considered under the Pradhan Mantri Jan Vikas Karyakram (PMJVK), a project must be proposed in areas certified by the State Level Committee (SLC) as Minority Concentrated Areas (MCAs), where the minority population exceeds 25% in a 15 km radius [1]. The project must focus on infrastructure development such as schools, health centers, community halls, and sanitation facilities to address socio-economic gaps in minority communities [2].  

**Key Requirements**  
- The project must be sustainable with clear provisions for recurring costs and maintenance.  
- It should align with the State’s Perspective Plan (2021–2026) and Annual Implementation Plan.  
- The project site must have a **Land Availability Certificate** and be approved by the SLC.  

**Documents Needed**  
- Preliminary Project Report (PPR)  
- Certificate for Minority Concentration Area  
- Land Availability Certificate  
- SLC Meeting Minutes and Approval Certificate  

**Next Steps**  
Contact your State/UT Minority Welfare Department for guidance on submitting proposals through the PMJVK online portal.

GQA-007.question: What is the requirement for a candidate to be eligible for the Rajiv Gandhi National Fellowship For Scheduled Caste Candidates?
GQA-007.reference_answer: The candidate must belong to SC/ST and have passed the Post Graduate Examination. They must also be registered for M.Phil./Ph.D.
GQA-007.answer:
**Recommended Scheme**  
The Rajiv Gandhi National Fellowship For Scheduled Caste Candidates [1] is designed for SC/ST candidates pursuing M.Phil. or Ph.D. studies.  

**Key Benefits & Eligibility**  
- **Eligibility**: Must belong to SC/ST, have passed post-graduation, and be registered for full-time M.Phil./Ph.D. [1].  
- **Reservation**: 3% of fellowships are reserved for PwD candidates from SC/ST categories [2].  
- **Exclusions**: Employees of educational institutions or government bodies are excluded [5].  

**Documents Needed**  
- Proof of SC/ST category [1].  
- Post-graduation certificate [1].  
- Registration proof for M.Phil./Ph.D. [1].  

**Next Steps**  
Apply online via the official portal [4]. Ensure you meet all criteria and submit required documents. For more details, visit [1].

To apply under the **Domestic Funding Of Foreign Training (DFFT)** scheme, you will need the following documents:  
- Valid Email ID, preferably NIC Email ID [1]  
- Service details of the officers [1]  
- Mobile Number [1]  
- Proof of achievements (if any) [1]

**Next Steps**  
Ensure you meet the eligibility criteria, which includes being an IAS officer, Group ‘A’ officer, or during deputation under the Central Staffing Scheme [3]. If you are unsure about your eligibility, provide more details so we can assist further.

GQA-009.question: What is the process to register a beneficiary under Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana - Gramin?
GQA-009.reference_answer: To register a beneficiary, visit the PMAY-G official website, fill in personal details, upload the Aadhaar consent form, search for the beneficiary, select to register, and fill in remaining details like ownership type and bank account information.
GQA-009.answer:
**Recommended Scheme**  
Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana - Gramin [1]  

**Key Benefits & Eligibility**  
This scheme provides financial assistance for constructing or repairing houses for rural poor households. Eligibility includes households without shelter, destitute individuals, manual scavengers, and others as specified [1].  

**Documents Needed**  
- MGNREGA job card number  
- Swachh Bharat Mission (SBM) number  
- Aadhaar card (for beneficiary identification)  
- Proof of income or social category (if applicable) [1]  

**Next Steps**  
1. Visit the official PMAY-G portal or contact the local Panchayat for assistance.  
2. Submit the required documents and details.  
3. Await approval and proceed with house construction or repair.  

For more details, visit [PMAY-G website](https://pmayg.nic.in).

GQA-010.question: What is the maximum subsidy amount a beneficiary can receive under the Development Support for Coffee in Traditional Areas: Water Augmentation scheme?
GQA-010.reference_answer: The maximum subsidy amount a beneficiary can receive is ₹2,50,000 per beneficiary for all components under the water augmentation scheme.
GQA-010.answer:
**Recommended Scheme**  
Development Support for Coffee in Traditional Areas: Water Augmentation [1]  

**Key Benefits & Eligibility**  
- Subsidy varies based on the size of the coffee holding, with higher subsidies for larger holdings [1].  
- Eligible for individual growers, joint owners, or family members (mother, father, wife, and children) with holdings up to 10 hectares [2].  

**Documents Needed**  
- Application and self-declaration form [1].  
- Proof of land ownership.  
- Quotation for machinery/equipment.  
- Self-prepared plan for water storage.  
- Bank passbook (preferably Aadhaar-seeded).  
- Invoice for irrigation equipment.  
- Work completion report and fund utilization certificate.  

**Next Steps**  
- Confirm if you are a farmer, as this scheme is specifically for growers [1].  
- Gather required documents and apply through the [official portal](https://www.myscheme.gov.in/schemes/dsctawa).

GQA-014.answer:

GQA-015.question: What type of industry is eligible for the Testing Fee Reimbursement Scheme?
GQA-015.reference_answer: The applicant must have a micro or small scale industry.
GQA-015.answer:
**Schemes That May Suit You**  
- **Testing Fee Reimbursement Scheme** [1] **NEEDS_MORE_INFO**: SC/ST owned micro or small enterprises can get 80% reimbursement on testing fees for quality checks [2].  
- **Scheme for Reimbursement of Testing and Certification Charges for Start-ups and Telecom MSEs** [4] **NEEDS_MORE_INFO**: Start-ups and telecom MSEs can get partial reimbursement for testing and certification charges.  

**Key Benefits & Eligibility**  
- Testing fees for raw materials, semi-finished, and finished products are covered.  
- Only SC/ST MSEs or start-ups in telecom/ICT are eligible.  

**Documents Needed**  
- Self-certified UAM & GST, PAN card, caste certificate, and testing reports.  

**Next Steps**  
Please clarify your social category (SC/ST) and whether you are an MSME or start-up. This will help narrow down the best scheme for you.  

What type of help are you looking for?

GQA-016.question: What document must be submitted by the interns at the end of their study under the Programme For Internship For LL.B./ LL.M./ Environmental Studies/ Research Students?
GQA-016.reference_answer: The interns must present a research paper/report on a selected topic and prepare notes on it for submission to the concerned officer.
GQA-016.answer:
**Documents Needed**  
At the end of their study, interns must submit a **research paper/report** on a selected topic. This document is required for evaluation and suggestions by the Commission [1].  

**Key Benefits & Eligibility**  
- **Certificate**: A certificate will be issued to the intern after evaluation of the research paper [2].  
- **Guide**: Each intern is assigned a guide for their study during the internship [2].  

**Next Steps**  
Ensure you prepare the research paper as per the guidelines. If you are a student pursuing LL.B./LL.M./Environmental Studies/Research, you may apply by submitting your application by 1st February (Summer) or 1st October (Winter) [1].

GQA-017.question: Can I include the cost of a long lease workshed in my project cost under the Pradhan Mantri Formalisation Of Micro Food Processing Enterprises scheme?
GQA-017.reference_answer: Yes, the cost of a long lease or rental workshed can be included in the project cost, but the lease rental should be for a maximum period of 3 years.
GQA-017.answer:
**Recommended Scheme**  
Pradhan Mantri Formalisation Of Micro Food Processing Enterprises (PMFMPE) [1]  

**Key Benefits & Eligibility**  
- Provides credit-linked subsidies up to ₹10,000 crores over five years [2].  
- Supports 2,00,000 micro food processing units with financial and infrastructural assistance.  
- Eligible entities include Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs), Self-Help Groups (SHGs), cooperatives, and existing micro food processing units.  

**Documents Needed**  
- Application must be submitted online [4].  
- Details of the project, including cost breakdown, must be provided.  

**Next Steps**  
- Clarify if your project involves a long lease workspace.  
- Ensure the workspace cost aligns with the scheme’s focus on food processing infrastructure.  
- Submit your application through the official portal [4].  

For precise guidance, consult the scheme’s eligibility criteria [1].

GQA-018.question: What is the total token stipend amount for the Scheme of Internship for Post-Graduate/Research Students?
GQA-018.reference_answer: The total token stipend is ₹10,000/-, paid in two installments of ₹5,000/- each.
GQA-018.answer:

The Scheme of Internship for Post-Graduate/Research Students offers a token stipend.  

**Key Benefits & Eligibility**  
- **Stipend**: A token stipend of ₹10,000/- (consolidated) is paid to selected interns on successful completion of the internship [1].  
- **Eligibility**: Open to post-graduate/research students in Statistics, Mathematical Statistics, Operations Research, Economics, Demography, or related fields from recognized universities/institutions [1].  

**Next Steps**  
To apply, ensure you meet the eligibility criteria and prepare the required documents. Visit the official scheme page for detailed application instructions [1].

GQA-019.question: What specific amenities are provided to tourists under the HRIDAY: Heritage City Development & Augmentation Yojana scheme?
GQA-019.reference_answer: Tourists are provided with improved signage, interpretation centres, and guided tours under the HRIDAY scheme.
GQA-019.answer:
**Recommended Scheme**  
HRIDAY: Heritage City Development & Augmentation Yojana [1]  

**Key Benefits for Tourists**  
- **Improved Safety & Accessibility**: Heritage cities become safer and more accessible, enhancing the visitor experience.  
- **Tourism Growth**: Increased foot traffic and market opportunities for heritage-related businesses like hotels, handicrafts, and cultural events.  
- **Cultural Preservation**: Support for traditional crafts and skills, benefiting local artisans and promoting cultural heritage.  
- **Infrastructure Development**: Enhanced urban planning and governance for heritage areas, leading to better facilities for tourists.  

**Documents Needed**  
- No documents are required for this scheme [3].  

**Next Steps**  
Visit the official HRIDAY page [1] for more details on how to benefit from these amenities.

**Recommended Scheme**  
Financial Assistance For Promotion Of Guru-Shishya Parampara (Repertory Grant) [1]

- Shisya/Artists receive financial support based on specific criteria.

- Proof of uploading videos of your Production/Function/Seminar on YouTube [1].  
- A certificate from the Principal of a school for organizing cultural activities [2].

- Confirm if you are a student or part of a performing arts group.  
- Prepare the required documents and submit them through the official process.

GQA-022.question: What is the maximum time gap allowed between the declaration of my final exam results and the start of the internship under the NITI Internship Scheme?
GQA-022.reference_answer: The maximum time gap allowed is six months.
GQA-022.answer:
**Maximum Time Gap for NITI Internship Scheme**  
Under the NITI Internship Scheme, the time gap between the declaration of your final exam results and the start of the internship should not exceed six months. For example, if your results are declared in June, you can apply for the internship beginning as late as December [1].  

**Documents Needed**  
- No specific documents are required for the application, as the process is entirely online [2].  

**Next Steps**  
- Visit the official website [https://workforindia.niti.gov.in/intern/InternshipEntry/PCInternshipEntry.aspx](https://workforindia.niti.gov.in/intern/InternshipEntry/PCInternshipEntry.aspx) to apply online during the specified months.  
- Ensure your final exam results are declared within six months of your desired internship start date.

- **Feedback** on the program experience to the Head of the Functional Wing/Field Office [1].  

These documents are mandatory for interns under the **Student Internship Programme** [1].  

**Next Steps**  
Visit the official CAG website for updates and apply via the provided Google Form [1].

GQA-025.question: What is the maximum incentive amount for completing a DeepSkilling – Free Pathway course under the FutureSkills Prime Incentive Program?
GQA-025.reference_answer: The maximum incentive for completing a DeepSkilling – Free Pathway course is ₹1,000, provided the Subscriber/beneficiary enrols for the next paid course with a cost greater or equal to ₹1,000.
GQA-025.answer:
**Maximum Incentive for DeepSkilling – Free Pathway**  
For completing a DeepSkilling – Free Pathway course under the FutureSkills Prime Incentive Program, the maximum incentive is ₹1,000 [1]. This incentive is provided if the learner enrolls in a paid course with a fee of ₹1,000 or more within 180 days of completing the free course [2].  

**Documents Needed**  
- Aadhaar Card  
- Bank Account Statement (with IFSC code)  
- Course Completion Certificate  
- Assessment Completion Certificate  

**Next Steps**  
1. Complete the free course and assessment.  
2. Enroll in a paid course within 180 days.  
3. Apply for the incentive through the FutureSkills Prime platform.  

For more details, visit [https://www.myscheme.gov.in/schemes/fspip](https://www.myscheme.gov.in/schemes/fspip).

- **Post Matric Scholarship Scheme For The Students Belonging To Scheduled Tribe For Studies In India** [NEEDS_MORE_INFO] – Offers financial support for SC/ST students pursuing post-matric courses in recognized institutions [3].

GQA-027.question: What is the deadline for submitting a life certificate for subsequent grants under the RMEWF-Financial Assistance For Ex-Servicemen In Penury scheme?
GQA-027.reference_answer: The life certificate must be submitted between 01 Dec and 31 Mar of the current financial year.

GQA-058.question: What is the maximum percentage of OBC (non-creamy layer) and poor general candidates allowed under the Coaching Schemes For Sc/st/obc (non-creamy Layer) & Minority Students For Universities?
GQA-058.reference_answer: The maximum percentage of OBC (non-creamy layer) and poor general candidates allowed is up to 40%.
GQA-058.answer:
**Schemes That May Suit You**  
- **Coaching Schemes For Sc/st/obc (non-creamy Layer) & Minority Students For Universities** [1] – **Needs More Info**: Offers financial assistance to universities with a sufficient number of SC, ST, and minority students, and allows up to 40% OBC (non-creamy layer) and poor general candidates if SC/ST/minority representation is insufficient.  
- **Free Coaching for SCs, OBCs and beneficiaries of PM CARES Children Scheme** [2] – **Needs More Info**: Provides free coaching for SC, OBC, and PM CARES beneficiaries, with a 70:30 SC:OBC ratio, and 30% female reservation.  

The maximum percentage of OBC (non-creamy layer) and poor general candidates allowed under the first scheme is **up to 40%**, but only if there is insufficient representation of SC, ST, and minority students [1].
